summary: Intermittent 403s for impersonated admin calls after projected service-account token rotation in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403 Forbidden responses when the Redwood control plane attempts to perform admin-level operations using impersonation (service-account token exchange) after projected token rotation on their private deployment. Impact: Admin console actions (user role changes, policy updates) and automated role-sync jobs fail intermittently for a subset of users, causing delayed user provisioning and blocked audit uploads. Environment: Private deployment (VPC) for Acme Health; Redwood control plane communicates with customer-managed auth-service that projects Kubernetes service account tokens into a sidecar volume. Problem first seen after IdP and K8s token lifetime changes on 2026-03-09.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer rotates projected service-account token TTL from 6h -> 15m on their cluster (k8s projected token).
2) Initiate admin action from Console that requires admin impersonation (e.g., add role binding via Console UI or run role-sync job).
3) Observe request path: Console -> Redwood control plane -> private auth-proxy -> exchange projected token for impersonation token -> call admin API -> sometimes 403 returned.
4) Reproduce attempts show that retrying the same operation immediately sometimes succeeds (race window).
logs: auth-proxy: 2026-03-09T14:02:12Z WARN token-exchange: token exp (iat/exp mismatch) detected for svcacct:acme-admin projected: token_k8s_mount_abc123
control-plane: 2026-03-09T14:02:12Z ERROR impersonation: upstream 403 from auth backend (reason=invalid_audience) request_id=rp-3f9a
console: 2026-03-09T14:02:13Z INFO retrying impersonation attempt (attempt=2) -> success
kubelet: 2026-03-09T14:02:11Z INFO token reviewer validated token with bound_sa=acme-admin ttl_remaining_seconds=120
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: projected token rotation shortened TTL introduces a race where the control plane reads a just-rotated token from the sidecar volume while the IdP/token reviewer has not yet accepted the new token binding, causing audience or jti mismatches.
Observed pattern: failures cluster around rotation window and affect only admin-impersonation flows that use token-exchange. Non-impersonated API calls from standard service tokens unaffected.
Reproduced internally by simulating projected token TTL=15m on staging private cluster. Saw deterministic 403s when token was read within 30s after rotation event.
Auth backend returns 403 with subcode 'invalid_audience' or 'jti_mismatch' in logs for failed exchanges. Token reviewer logs show transient validation failures for new tokens until cache refresh.

Related to previous tickets SUP-84721 (service-account impersonation rotation failure) but this case differs: failure is caused by short projected TTL + local filesystem propagation delay + token-reviewer cache TTL (customer-side).
comments: Ava Thompson (Support): Customer reports ~15% of admin actions failing since they changed projected token TTL. They've paused rotation and failures rate dropped.

Marcus Li (SRE): Investigating token exchange path and caching in auth-proxy. Added increased logging and a request_id trace to isolate timing. Suspect race between kube projected token refresh and token-reviewer cache TTL on the IdP side.
Priya Natarajan (Customer Success): Noted customer cannot extend projected TTL due to security policy. Customer requests guidance for a config-based mitigation in Redwood while they revisit policy.
James Parker (Acme Health, Customer): We see failures mostly during our nightly key rotation window. Can Redwood add a small retry/backoff or validate token freshness before exchange?

Marcus Li (SRE): Proposed mitigation: 1) add short deterministic retry (3 attempts with 200ms jitter) on 403 with subcodes 'invalid_audience'/'jti_mismatch' during impersonation exchange, 2) optionally verify token 'iat' and wait up to 1s if token age < 5s before attempting exchange. Will validate with staging. Filing follow-up internal task to implement guarded retry.
Ava Thompson (Support): Scheduled call with customer 2026-03-13 to validate staging patch. Tracking SLA milestones.
resolution: Investigating - temporary mitigation recommended (pause aggressive projected TTL reduction). Patch under test: guarded retry on impersonation token-exchange and 1s token-stabilization wait when token iat is very recent.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Implemented guarded retry in auth-proxy branch and validated on staging with projected TTL=15m; observed failure rate drop to ~0.5% from 15%.
2026-03-12: Coordinated with customer to re-run their rotation in staging; recommended final rollout with feature flag off-by-default for private deployments in case of policy constraints.
Follow-up: engineering task INT-1189 created to add configurable token-stabilization delay and document guidance for projected token TTLs in private deployments.
